title: Decision: Diageo Scotland Limited v The Coal Authority
text:
LANDS TRIBUNAL FOR SCOTLAND

Citation: [2025] LTS 23 , Case reference: LTS/COMP/2023/0002

NOTE (EXPENSES)

Tribunal members: Mr R A Smith KC , Mrs D Lovell

Diageo Scotland Limited
Applicant
against
The Coal Authority
Respondent

Subjects: Bonnybridge Bonded Warehouses, 151 Glasgow Road, Dennyloanhead, Bonnybridge

1 October 2025

[1] This note deals with a motion for expenses following the preliminary evidential hearing on time bar, which we heard on 19 March 2025. We are dealing with the motion by means of written submissions. In our opinion of 17 April we found that the claim for remedial action in respect of damage occurring prior to 2009 was time barred, and we upheld the respondent’s submission in that respect. However, we allowed the application to proceed in respect of the 2017 damage and in respect of the sinkhole, which claims on the agreed hypothesis of fact, we accepted were not time barred.

[2] In these circumstances the applicant seeks the expenses for the conduct and preparation of the evidential hearing and for the site visit which preceded it on 17 March 2025. The applicant also seeks sanction for the employment of senior counsel, and for expenses to be taxed upon the Court of Session scale.

[3] The respondent submitted that there had been divided success in that the respondent’s submission regarding the pre‑2009 damage to warehouses 1 and 6 had been upheld. There should accordingly be no expenses due to or by either party. In any event, should the Tribunal consider that the applicant had enjoyed a greater degree of success, it was suggested that an award of expenses in its favour should be abated by 50%. The respondent also submitted that the expenses of the site visit should be reserved, since the viewing would be useful for future hearings and not just the preliminary hearing on time bar. The motion seeking sanction for senior counsel was not opposed.

[4] The applicant submitted that it had enjoyed substantial success, since the respondent had submitted that the whole claim was time barred and there was no reason not to apply the general rule that expenses followed success. A party did not need to win on all points to be substantially successful. Only on the morning of the hearing did the respondent accept that the claim in respect of the sinkhole was not time-barred. The main finding by the tribunal was that a 1991 Act claim for subsistence damage did not require to be treated as a once and for all claim, and that the claim for the 2017 settlement damage fell to be treated as a separate cause of action. This was the issue which took up most of the preparation and hearing time and, as would have been apparent at the site visit, constituted the more serious damage. The pre-2009 damage was of relatively minor significance, but evidence would still need to be heard about it to distinguish it from later damage, so there was no substantial advantage in the resolution of that part of the claim. In any event a modification as high as 50% could not be justified.

[5] It was further submitted that the site visit was an integral part of the preliminary hearing. It was necessary to assist the tribunal’s understanding of the factual position and arguments relating to time bar. It was likely that the tribunal would need to make a further visit once the expert reports came in from both sides, to assist its appraisal of matters on the ground. It was inherent to the case that it was not possible for there to be an unaccompanied inspection.

[6] Sanction for senior counsel should be allowed as the legal issues were novel and complex, and involved consideration of old loss of support cases in the light of modern authorities. Both sides had instructed senior counsel. The extent and cost of remedial works was likely to be substantial, justifying expenses being awarded upon the Court of Session scale.

Decision

[7] We consider this to be a case of divided success. The respondent’s success has been relatively minor, but has not been insignificant. The pre-2009 damage had affected the applicant’s operations at the site to some extent. On the other hand, the 2017 damage was more serious, and the arguments at the hearing concentrated on the “single loss” argument, on which the applicants succeeded.

[8] In these circumstances we shall allow the applicants their expenses of preparation and conducting the hearing, modified by a factor of 20%, to reflect the respondent’s minor success. We agree that the site visit should be included in the expenses allowed, for the reasons given by the applicants, including the point that it is likely that a further visit will be required. We shall sanction the employment of senior counsel, and find that expenses should be assessed on the scale applicable to the Court of Session.
